# zenfra_stack_dependency (Resource)

Manages a dependency between two stacks: after each successful tracked apply of the parent stack, Zenfra starts a run of the child stack. Changing the parent or the child replaces the dependency. The API refuses a dependency on the stack itself, a duplicate, one that would close a cycle, and one past the depth or fan-out limits; the refusal is reported at apply. Import with `<child_stack_id>/<dependency_id>`: a dependency is read through its child stack, so the child's id is part of the import id.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# After each successful tracked apply of the network stack, start a run of the app stack.
resource "zenfra_stack_dependency" "app_after_network" {
  parent_stack_id = zenfra_stack.network.id
  child_stack_id  = zenfra_stack.app.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `child_stack_id` (String) The stack that runs after the parent applies. Changing it replaces the dependency.
- `parent_stack_id` (String) The stack whose successful apply starts a run of the child. Changing it replaces the dependency.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the dependency starts runs of the child. Defaults to `true`. A new dependency is always created enabled, so `false` is refused when the dependency is created or replaced: create it enabled and set `enabled = false` in a later apply.

### Read-Only

- `activated_at` (String) When the dependency was last enabled (RFC 3339), set at creation and at every enable.
- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the dependency.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import zenfra_stack_dependency.app_after_network $CHILD_STACK_ID/$DEPENDENCY_ID
```
